cfs.subject: command resolution order
cfs.statement: **Command resolution order (CF-DSC-001).** For one name the searcher tries, in this order and returning the first match that is allowed: (1) **alias** (a match whose visibility does not allow the caller's origin is skipped and the search continues with functions); (2) **function / filter / configuration**; (3) **cmdlet** (a module-qualified name `Module\Cmdlet` matches only cmdlets of that module; with several cmdlets of the same name in different modules, the first in table order is returned unless all scopes are searched); (4) if application or external-script types are allowed: a name that is a *qualified provider path* is resolved as a path; then an absolute path to an existing file; then the file system search of each `PATH` directory in order (for a name with a directory part: only that directory); then a PowerShell-relative path (name starting with `.`, `~` or `\`). Within one directory the candidate file names are, in order: the name itself first if it already has an extension; `name.ps1` when external scripts are allowed (also `.psm1` and `.psd1` in non-discovery searches); on Windows every `PATHEXT` extension when applications are allowed; then the bare name if not yet added. A `.ps1` file becomes an external script; any other existing file becomes an application. If the normal search fails and the name contains neither `-` nor `\`, the lookup is repeated once with the name prefixed with `Get-`. If still unresolved, module-qualified names trigger module auto-loading, and (with `$PSModuleAutoLoadingPreference` = `All`, the default) other names trigger module auto-discovery against the module analysis cache; then the *command-not-found* handler runs; then a `CommandNotFoundException` is raised. In a session whose origin is `Runspace`, application and external-script types are removed from the search when the session state has no allowed applications or scripts, and a name with a directory part must match an allow-list entry (prefix match, or the list is exactly `*`).
cfs.label: FACT-SRC

deviations.baseline_behavior: Unknown command names trigger module auto-discovery by analyzing every module file on PSModulePath.
deviations.proposed_behavior: Resolve through an explicit signed command index refreshed on module install/update; keep module-qualified auto-load.
deviations.benefit: Faster misses, no file scans on typos, auditable resolution.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Modules not indexed are not auto-loaded until indexed.

deviations.baseline_behavior: Native argument passing has three styles (Legacy, Standard, Windows) with a name-based list of legacy programs.
deviations.proposed_behavior: List-based passing only, with a per-command opt-in for raw command lines.
deviations.benefit: Removes the quoting ambiguity and the legacy program list.
deviations.compatibility_cost: Scripts relying on Legacy re-quoting need the opt-in.
